name: AI News
blurb: Daily AI news from the publishers who broke it, split into headline coverage of the field and vendor announcements from the companies building it. Every story links to the original source, and any claim quoted in our coverage is cross-referenced against the laws, lawsuits, companies, tools, papers, and people already tracked in this atlas.

domains.name: AI Headline News
domains.blurb: The day's most consequential AI stories across law, policy, research, safety, and society, curated from 34 vetted feeds. Each item carries the original publisher link and a note on how it connects to the bills, cases, and frameworks tracked elsewhere on this site.

domains.name: AI Vendor News
domains.blurb: Product launches, model releases, pricing changes, and company announcements from the AI vendors themselves. Each item links to the vendor's original announcement and cross-references the company's profile in our AI Companies directory where one exists.

domains.name: This Week in AI
domains.blurb: A weekly record of what moved in AI policy and litigation, permalinked by ISO week.

domains.name: AI Historical Timeline
domains.blurb: From the 1940s to the present: Turing, the perceptron, expert systems, backpropagation, deep learning, AlexNet, transformers, and what followed.

reading.body:
The site tracks 484 pages of daily AI headline coverage curated from 34 vetted news feeds, with each story linked to original sources and cross-referenced against laws, lawsuits, companies, and research tracked elsewhere in the atlas.

The volume of coverage reflects the density of consequential AI developments across law, policy, research, safety, and society. Most stories originate from independent publishers rather than vendor announcements, which occupy only one page. This distribution suggests that regulatory and societal impacts are outpacing product releases in news value, or that the feeds selected prioritize these categories.

The cross-referencing system means readers can trace how a single news item connects to the infrastructure of AI governance: which bills it affects, which lawsuits it may influence, which companies it involves. This matters for understanding AI scaling because regulation and policy shape what infrastructure can be built. A constraint imposed by law or litigation is a constraint on buildings and power just as much as a material shortage is.

The data does not show which stories move most frequently, which topics dominate, or how coverage has shifted over time. It captures what exists, not what is emphasized or what patterns are emerging.
